title: Defence Legislation Amendment (Military Justice Enhancements—Inspector-General ADF) Bill 2014
short_title: Defence Legislation Amendment (Military Justice Enhancements—Inspector-General ADF) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would change how the Australian Defence Force handles internal reviews and complaints.
It would give the Inspector-General ADF more independence and clearer legal powers to conduct investigations and inquiries.
Witnesses giving evidence to the Inspector-General ADF would be protected from having that evidence used against them, except in perjury cases.
changes: Clarifies that the Inspector-General ADF operates independently from the chain of command.
Allows the minister to order the Inspector-General ADF to look into a Defence Force matter.
Creates a legal basis for regulations that remove a witness's right to refuse to answer questions on self-incrimination grounds, with a ban on using that evidence against the witness.
Requires the Inspector-General ADF to produce an annual report for Parliament.
Lets the Inspector-General ADF stop an inquiry or investigation ordered by the Chief of the Defence Force if it is no longer warranted.
Gives the Inspector-General ADF a statutory role in managing how service-related deaths are investigated and how grievances are handled.
summary.affected: Australian Defence Force members and witnesses appearing before the Inspector-General ADF.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Andrews
speeches.brief: The Defence Legislation Amendment (Military Justice Enhancements-Inspector-General ADF) Bill 2014 was introduced to strengthen the independence of the Inspector-General of the Australian Defence Force and reform redress of grievance, investigation and inquiry processes. Key changes include preventing witness evidence obtained by abrogating self-incrimination privilege from being used in service tribunals or civilian courts, and removing the automatic requirement for a statutory inquiry into all service-related deaths, instead referring them to the Inspector-General for review.

speeches.speaker: David Feeney
speeches.brief: The speaker announced Labour's support for the Defence Legislation Amendment (Military Justice Enhancements-Inspector-General ADF) Bill 2014, which enhances the independence of the Inspector-General of the Australian Defence Force by separating it from the military chain of command, expands investigative powers, requires annual reports tabled in parliament, and includes protections against self-incrimination for witnesses.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Defence Legislation Amendment (Military Justice Enhancements-Inspector-General ADF) Bill 2014, arguing it strengthens the Inspector-General's independence, powers, and accountability. The speech noted that in 2013–14 the Inspector-General received 60 inquiry submissions, conducted 49 unit audits, and made 714 recommendations.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Defence Legislation Amendment (Military Justice Enhancements-Inspector-General ADF) Bill 2014 expands and strengthens the independence of the Inspector-General of the Australian Defence Force, consolidating functions and ensuring direct reporting to parliament. The bill addresses the redress of grievance process, grants the Inspector-General powers to compel witness testimony with use immunity, and implements recommendations from 17 reviews since 1994, including those following the 2011 ADFA Skype incident.
